B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: PitchBook says its direct MCP capability is being tested and is expected to use consumption-based pricing; the broader pricing structure is still being evaluated. Its August 2026 investor Q&A says paid subscribers could access Premium Connectors at no additional charge at that time. The vendor says Data MCP is available to customers upon request.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: PitchBook license required for Premium Connector use: seat-based, unlimited, or trial. No public price amount was found.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The vendor distinguishes Premium Connector access from a separate direct MCP capability expected to use consumption-based pricing. Premium Connector access was described as included at no extra charge for paying subscribers at the time of the August 2026 Q&A; expanded access was being piloted and required at least one full PitchBook platform license, with connector-only seats possible.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. The reported tool set consists of read-style lookup and analysis actions; no write or destructive action appears in the published names/descriptions. Tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published in the examined lists.
2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview/confirm flow was found. Claude's documented approval setting is a client permission setting; users can change it from “Needs approval” to “Always allow.”
3. OAuth metadata lists scopes openid, profile, email, offline_access; these are identity/profile scopes, not explicit data-operation scopes. PitchBook says connector access is tied to each user's permissions and SSO. Platform admins may need to enable integrations and data sets. Token expiry/lifetime and redirect-URI approval details were not found.
4. No read-only mode, tool filtering, or per-region endpoint variation was established for the supplied endpoint. A separate external gateway describes selectable custom toolsets and persistent toolset endpoints. Partner platform enablement can vary.
5. PitchBook says data is returned according to each user's permissions. No MCP-specific masking, PII exclusion, or field-level protection behavior was found.
6. No rate limits or result-size caps were found for the supplied endpoint. Glean, Rogo, and Copilot connector guides each state limits of 150 calls per hour and 300 per day for those integrations; this is not evidence of the supplied endpoint's quota. No per-call MCP price was established.
7. Tool schemas and server-side argument validation/correction were not published.
8. MCP-specific audit trails, logging, and telemetry behavior were not found. PitchBook's general privacy policy describes collection of authorized-user IP, location, and service/session usage information.
9. No feedback, rating, survey, or reporting tool appears in the published 16-tool directory list. Vendor materials describe PitchBook data and proprietary insights as grounded/validated; no MCP upsell result was found. The policy documents pricing evaluation at product level.
10. No MCP-served skills were documented. PitchBook's separate PitchBook AI product has Skills and Agents; these are described as in-platform features, not tools on this endpoint. Partner docs and third-party descriptions contain behavioral guidance, but it is not shown as server-enforced.
11. No evidence found that previous agent behavior changes future tool outputs, resources, or prompts.
12. PitchBook offers several partner integrations and a separately announced Data MCP product. The external gateway page describes optional custom toolsets and endpoints; their relation to this endpoint's architecture/tool set is unclear.
13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or other universal escape-hatch tool appears in the published list.

The supplied hostname is distinct from the premium.mcp.pitchbook.com endpoint shown in third-party listings for the Claude Premium Connector; PitchBook also publishes a separate external gateway page for configurable toolsets. The exact relationship and tool-set boundaries between these surfaces are not documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: No official complete tool list for the supplied endpoint was found. PitchBook's ChatGPT help page officially names pitchbook_get_reports_analysis; its Semaverse guide states that 12 tools are available and names two human-readable examples, but does not enumerate all names. Agent Discoverability lists 16 exact tool names for the PitchBook ChatGPT app, dated around the analysis date; these are included as third-party names. The resulting actions.json contains 17 entries: the one exact official name plus those 16 catalogue names. ToolJunction lists 11 tools for premium.mcp.pitchbook.com, a separate host; Claude's directory also points to that separate host. No claim is made that partner-specific lists are identical to the supplied endpoint.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: PitchBook advises the user to specify “Using PitchBook data as the source” to ensure a response contains only PitchBook's verified proprietary data. The Semaverse guide recommends Deep Analysis for complex research and says it can systematically use multiple PitchBook tools; its tip says Deep Analysis is best used with investment Memo templates and instructions. These are prompt/client guidance; no endpoint enforcement is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: PitchBook says connector responses follow each user's permissions and that SSO ties access to those permissions. It describes the connection as secure and states that only approved AI platforms, such as authorized enterprise accounts, can interact with PitchBook data. Its general privacy policy describes security measures and retention as necessary for stated uses. No MCP-specific data retention, training, or audit commitments were found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes PitchBook Data MCP as providing native, secure access to a subset of its company, deal, investor, and fund data, with grounding and accuracy consistent with the PitchBook platform. It says the direct Data MCP is live and available to customers upon request.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth protection is evidenced by endpoint metadata. PitchBook's user-permission and SSO statements are documented, but the implementation details are not public. Secure/grounded-data promises and prompt advice are not independently verifiable from public server code. No endpoint code or tool schemas were available to test the stated controls.

contradictions: PitchBook's Semaverse help page states that 12 tools are available and gives two human-readable examples; the Agent Discoverability ChatGPT-app listing reports 16 tools, while ToolJunction lists 11 tools for premium.mcp.pitchbook.com. These counts refer to different partner listings/endpoints or configurations and do not establish one common count for the supplied endpoint.

The official ChatGPT help page names pitchbook_get_reports_analysis, which is not among the 16 names in the third-party Agent Discoverability list. It is included separately as an official action; the difference may reflect different dates, availability, or partner-specific tool exposure.

The supplied endpoint is mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp; the Claude connector directory and ToolJunction identify premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp. The official materials reviewed do not clarify whether these endpoints share the same tools or implementation.
observations_for_research: The OAuth scope list consists of identity/profile scopes (openid, profile, email, offline_access); the vendor separately describes data permissions as inherited from the user's PitchBook access.

Vendor documentation describes administrative activation of new ChatGPT data sets/tools, while the OAuth metadata exposes a general authorization flow. The effect of each control on the supplied endpoint's available tools is not specified.

The vendor distinguishes Premium Connector access from a direct Data MCP capability and has stated that the latter is expected to use consumption-based pricing; exact entitlement boundaries and endpoint mapping remain unclear.
